scenes.role: reference opening and ordinary wants
actions: Mira hopes to earn trust; Kit settles Pip beside the bedrolls.
consequences: Establishes the siblings' different wants and shared campsite.
prose_obligations: Show ordinary family life and distinct sibling motives.

scenes.role: reference setup for the missing toy
prerequisites: The siblings are together before supper.
actions: Kit carries Pip while helping Mira with camp chores.
consequences: Pip can slip from Kit's jacket pocket without either child seeing.
prose_obligations: Make the later loss an ordinary accident, not carelessness as a moral flaw.

scenes.role: essential inciting encounter
prerequisites: Pip is missing.
actions: Kit checks the sleeping bags and admits he is frightened.
consequences: The siblings share the goal of finding Pip before supper.
prose_obligations: Make Kit's fear concrete and let Mira respond with care.

scenes.role: reference vow consolidated into the reveal and borrowing plays
prerequisites: Kit has admitted the loss.
actions: Mira promises to help rather than dismiss the toy.
consequences: Her promise becomes a motive for the search.
prose_obligations: Avoid treating a child's comfort object as trivial.

scenes.role: essential borrowed-object encounter
prerequisites: The lantern is with Dad; the children are at camp.
actions: Mira asks Dad to borrow the battery lantern.
consequences: Custody changes while ownership remains Dad's.
prose_obligations: Show permission and a clear expectation that the lantern comes back.

scenes.role: borrowed-object responsibility consolidated into the borrowing play
prerequisites: Dad agrees to lend the lantern.
actions: Mira promises to bring it back before supper.
consequences: The ending must return the useful object, not merely mention it.
prose_obligations: Preserve the distinction between borrowing and owning.

scenes.role: local physical action consolidated into borrowing
prerequisites: The lantern has charge.
actions: Mira switches on the lantern.
consequences: The light is available for the search.
prose_obligations: A functioning lantern must have a plausible power source.

scenes.role: reference fear beat and optional vignette setup
prerequisites: The lantern is lit; Kit has disclosed his fear.
actions: The children see their shadows stretch on the canvas.
consequences: Creates an opportunity for a brave, affectionate response.
prose_obligations: Keep the fear rooted in ordinary evening shadows.

scenes.role: optional character vignette
prerequisites: The lantern has been borrowed and the fox has been discussed.
actions: Mira makes a fox shape; Kit joins in and accepts the lantern.
consequences: Kit's courage persists into the search; he can carry the lantern.
prose_obligations: Show a small earned change, not a sudden cure for fear.

scenes.role: reference clue, consolidated into the reveal
prerequisites: Kit reflects on when he last had Pip.
actions: Kit recalls the tent edge, while remaining uncertain.
consequences: The remembered spot can differ from Pip's actual location.
prose_obligations: Make mistaken memory understandable rather than arbitrary.

scenes.role: reference clue represented by validated parameters and search play
prerequisites: Kit remembers walking near the ferns in his jacket.
actions: The children consider another possible place Pip fell.
consequences: A second search can resolve a mistaken first memory.
prose_obligations: Connect the alternate site to a plausible prior action.

scenes.role: optional route vignette
prerequisites: The children are still at camp; Dad can see the path.
actions: Dad clips reflective tabs along the return route.
consequences: The siblings can use the markers if the lantern runs out.
prose_obligations: Make the path aid visible before it is used.

scenes.role: consequential choice encounter
prerequisites: Kit has shared a remembered site; the lantern is in hand.
actions: Mira chooses a careful single search or a second sweep if resources allow.
consequences: The policy trades search chances against keeping light and time for the way back.
prose_obligations: Let the choice affect actions and outcomes, not just dialogue.

scenes.role: search transition consolidated into the search-plan scene
prerequisites: The siblings have agreed where to start.
actions: They follow Kit's remembered route together.
consequences: Sibling and lantern locations remain continuous.
prose_obligations: No teleporting between campsite locations.

scenes.role: essential local search action
prerequisites: The lantern is lit and has charge.
actions: The siblings inspect the first place Kit recalls.
consequences: Consumes lantern charge and some remaining daylight.
prose_obligations: Record whether the toy is there; do not imply an unplayed search.

scenes.role: complication consolidated into the search outcome
prerequisites: The remembered site is not Pip's actual location.
actions: The first sweep finds ordinary camp debris, not the fox.
consequences: Mira must decide whether resources justify looking farther.
prose_obligations: Let disappointment deepen the stakes without blaming Kit.

scenes.role: consequential local choice
prerequisites: The first sweep missed; another sweep is allowed by the chosen policy and resources.
actions: Mira spends remaining light to inspect the other site, or stops.
consequences: The choice can find Pip or end the search with a safe return.
prose_obligations: Explain the ordinary cost of going farther after dusk.

scenes.role: essential payoff when the toy is present
prerequisites: The siblings inspect the actual site.
actions: They lift a rainfly or leaf and recover Pip.
consequences: The fox moves from its physical hiding place into Kit's hands.
prose_obligations: Make the recovery earned by the enacted search.

scenes.role: essential return encounter
prerequisites: The search has ended, whether successful or not.
actions: The siblings follow the lantern, reflectors, daylight, or campfire glow.
consequences: They return safely; Kit is no longer left alone in the dark.
prose_obligations: Use only a route aid that was actually available.

scenes.role: borrowed-object payoff consolidated into both endings
prerequisites: The siblings are back at camp with the borrowed lantern.
actions: Mira returns the lantern to Dad.
consequences: Custody returns to its owner after the lantern has helped.
prose_obligations: Show both the object’s usefulness and its return.

scenes.role: earned success ending
prerequisites: Pip was physically recovered and the siblings returned safely.
actions: Kit settles Pip beside his bedroll; the lantern goes back to Dad.
consequences: The missing toy is home and Kit's fear has eased.
prose_obligations: Close both the search and Mira's care for Kit.

scenes.role: emotionally complete failure ending
prerequisites: The search ended without Pip and the siblings returned safely.
actions: Kit accepts a camp blanket and names his sadness without being alone.
consequences: The loss remains real, but the immediate fear is resolved.
prose_obligations: Do not promise that a future search will fix this ending.
